name: Street Custom 'Smoke Box' Improvised Concealment Generator
product_name: Street Custom 'Smoke Box' Improvised Concealment Generator
description: A repurposed theatrical fog machine loaded with an opaque chemical smoke compound that produces a dense white cloud obscuring a 15-meter area within 10 seconds. The Smoke Box is built from salvaged fog machines, modified vaporizer heating elements, or even pressurized cooking oil containers — any device that can rapidly aerosolize a liquid. The smoke compound is typically a mixture of glycol fog fluid and titanium dioxide powder that creates a cloud impenetrable to visible light and degraded for thermal imaging. Street operators use it for escape, ambush concealment, and preventing visual identification during operations.

specifications.operator visibility: Also zero — operator is equally blinded

story_hooks: A coordinated robbery used six Smoke Boxes simultaneously to blind an entire city block — the smoke coverage was so complete that surveillance footage shows nothing for four minutes across 20 cameras.
A modified Smoke Box has been developed that produces smoke with an embedded irritant — not enough to incapacitate, but enough to make anyone without eye protection unable to keep their eyes open.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian cylindrical device with jury-rigged construction — part theatrical equipment, part improvised weapon. The body shows visible welds, mismatched plating, and exposed heating coils. A large pressurized tank forms the core, with heating elements wrapped around it like mechanical tendrils. The nozzle is wide and flared, designed for maximum dispersal. Overall aesthetic is functional brutalism: no polish, all pragmatism.
physical_description.dimensions: 45cm tall, 20cm diameter cylinder — backpack or shoulder-carry sized
physical_description.weight_description: 2-3kg when full — handheld but requires stabilizing strap or mount when deployed
physical_description.primary_material: Salvaged stainless steel pressure vessel, aluminum heating jacket, rubber-coated steel trigger assembly
physical_description.finish: Bare metal with visible oxidation and heat-discoloration marks; welding seams prominent and unground; rubber grip sections worn glossy from use
physical_description.color_scheme: Metallic silver-grey with dark carbon scorching around heating coils; accents of burnt orange rust; matte black trigger guard and safety lever
physical_description.interface_elements: Pressure gauge (analog needle, red warning zone at 80PSI); manual ignition button (large, recessed, industrial); safety lever (flip-up); refill port with threaded brass cap; venting valve with manual release knob
distinctive_features: Visible braided metal heating coil wrapped in tight spirals around upper tank section
Handwritten pressure capacity markings (in marker) on side panel
Duct-taped wiring bundle running from ignition module to heating element
Custom-welded mounting bracket suggesting field modification
Scorch marks and chemical staining around nozzle outlet
Pressure relief tube venting downward with a small copper funnel
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Faded 'STREET CUSTOM' stencil on tank face; no regulatory stamps (intentionally removed or never present); handwritten serial number scratched into base plate
physical_description.condition_typical: Active use shows residual white powder coating on nozzle edges; faint chemical odor clings to exterior; pressure gauge needle sitting 40-60PSI range; trigger assembly shows minor corrosion from glycol exposure
